Volkswagen ID. Tiguan to Replace ID.4

September 28, 2026
Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 2:32
Instaread

It’s common for manufacturers to give their all-electric lineups a special name, something to denote these models from their traditional offerings. In the case of Volkswagen, their “ID” addon has been the key signifier; while other parts of the world have seen other ID models, the ID.4 kicked things off in the U.S. for 2021, followed by the ID. Buzz microbus.

These two have locked down VW’s electric U.S. portfolio, but next year will see a bit of a reset: Volkswagen is pulling the plug on the ID.4, and the ID.5 in other markets, to be replaced by the new, still camouflaged ID. Tiguan.

The full reveal of the ID. Tiguan will take place early in October, so we expect to learn more about its powertrain and features fairly soon; however, we’ll likely be deciphering a list of European specs, as the ID. Tiguan is said to launch in that market early 2027, its North American launch scheduled later in the year, though exactly when it to be determined.

The Tiguan name is a big one for Volkswagen, having produced more than 8.3 million units since its inception nearly two decades prior and reigning as Volkswagen’s best selling model worldwide. It should be noted that in their relatively short runs, the ID.4 and ID. 5 have accrued more than 950,000 deliveries, certainly no shortcoming.

That all said, it’s a reasonable approach to combine these two compact utilities under one popular name; in a way, giving would-be Tiguan buyers the choice of powertrain. How it lives up to previous expectations set forth by the ID.4 is anyone’s guess right now, though we suspect it’ll at least meet, if not supersede them. Currently, the ID.4 is available with either rear- or all-wheel drive, the former consisting of a single 282-horsepower electric motor and capable of 291 miles of range, the latter a 335-horsepower system made up of two motors with a max certified range of 263 miles.

Those range numbers are just a tad short of today’s standards, which we expect the ID. Tiguan will rectify, but the ID.4 has been a standout choice for EV buyers since its arrival, and has benefitted from occasional improvements since 2021. Not only that, but the ID.4 has been a huge investment in Volkswagen’s plant in Chattanooga, Tennessee. It’s unclear whether the ID. Tiguan will be assembled there as well, but it’s an impressive facility that we believe is certainly up to the task.
